title: 送柴侍御
author: 王昌龄
intro: A farewell poem that refuses to be sad: the rivers connect us, the same clouds and rain fall on us both, and the same bright moon shines on us — so how can we be in two different places?
analysis: 一般的送别诗都写离别的伤心，这首却反过来安慰朋友。王昌龄当时被贬到龙标（今湖南黔阳一带），朋友柴侍御要去武冈。第一句说：沅水的波浪一直通到武冈，两地有河相连。所以第二句说：送你走，我并不觉得有离别的悲伤。后两句是名句：两地之间的青山，共同承受着一样的云和雨；同一轮明月照着我们，怎么能说我们在两个地方呢？用“同”和“何曾是两乡”，把两地的距离一下子拉近了。其实正因为舍不得，才要这样劝慰对方——表面洒脱，底下是很深的情谊。后来日本长屋王赠给中国僧人的袈裟上绣着“山川异域，风月同天”，意思和这首诗很接近。
analysisEn: Most farewell poems dwell on the sadness of parting; this one turns it around and comforts the friend. Wang Changling had been demoted to Longbiao (in today’s western Hunan), and his friend Censor Chai was leaving for Wugang. The first line says the waves of the Yuan River flow all the way to Wugang — the two places are joined by water. So, line two: seeing you off, I don’t feel the pain of parting. The last two lines are the famous ones: the green hills between us share the same clouds and rain, and one bright moon shines on us both — how could we ever be in two separate places? With the words 同 (“the same”) and 何曾是两乡 (“when were we ever in two places?”) the distance shrinks to nothing. Of course, it is because he will miss his friend so much that he talks this way: light on the surface, deep friendship underneath. The line has a modern echo: in 2020, aid boxes sent from Japan to China carried the old phrase “mountains and rivers in different lands, wind and moon under the same sky”, which says much the same thing.
background: Wang Changling (c. 698–757) was a celebrated master of the quatrain. He wrote this while serving in exile as a minor official in Longbiao, in the remote south-west of today’s Hunan; nothing else is known of Censor Chai (侍御 is an official title).
pronunciation: 侍御 shì yù；沅水 yuán；武冈 gāng；一道 yī dào（不变调）。
version: 采用通行文本。首句《全唐诗》作“流水通波接武冈”，今通行选本多作“沅水通波接武冈”。

lines.py: yuán shuǐ tōng bō jiē wǔ gāng
lines.lit: The Yuan River’s waves flow through, joining Wugang;
lines.en: The Yuan River runs its waves all the way to Wugang;

lines.py: sòng jūn bù jué yǒu lí shāng
lines.lit: seeing you off, I do not feel the sorrow of parting.
lines.en: seeing you go, I don’t feel we are parting at all.

lines.py: qīng shān yī dào tóng yún yǔ
lines.lit: One range of green hills shares the same clouds and rain;
lines.en: One line of green hills, the same cloud and rain;

lines.py: míng yuè hé céng shì liǎng xiāng
lines.lit: under the bright moon, when were we ever in two places?
lines.en: one bright moon — how are we in two places?

words.en: waves flowing through, connected by water

words.note: 道：量词，今天也说“一道山梁”。

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 沅水连通两地，水把两个人连在一起，距离好像不存在了。
imagery.en: The Yuan River links the two towns — water joining the two friends, so the distance seems to vanish.

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 两地之间的青山共同承受云雨，暗示两人共同的命运和感情。
imagery.en: The green hills between them share the same clouds and rain — a shared fate, a shared feeling.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 同一轮明月照着两人，所以“何曾是两乡”，这是用月来安慰离别。
imagery.en: One moon shines on both of them, so how can they be apart? The moon turns parting into comfort.
